newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM says Peru hostage outcome unclear.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM says Peru hostage outcome unclear.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said on Saturday it was unclear how and when the 39-day-old Lima hostage crisis would end.
Asked by visiting South Korean President Kim Young-sam about the prospects of a solution to the hostage crisis, Hashimoto replied:"There is no clear outlook."

"When the incident was settled, Japan would do soul-searching, make thorough analysis and exchange information with South Korea," Hashimoto said during a lunch at this scenic resort city on Japan's southwestern island of Kyushu.
Hashimoto and Kim are holding a one-day summit meeting.
Details of the lunch conversation were released by Japanese officials.
Marxist rebels stormed the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima on December 17, taking more than 500 hostages and demanding the release of some 400 imprisoned comrades.
Alghough the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels have released most hostages, they still hold 73 captives.
South Korea's ambassador to Peru was among an early group of hostages released.
"This is an issue not only for Japan and Peru but also for the entire world," Kim said during the lunch meeting.
On Friday, the Peruvian government sought to unnerve the rebels by sending armoured cars rumbling past the ambassador's home for the first time since the siege began.
